promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority and edit target: keep every shape exactly
Image 2: Material, palette and finish reference only; not layout

Use case: sketch-to-render, game sprite sheet. Image 1 is the authoritative geometry guide and edit target: reskin it, keeping every shape exactly where and how big it is on the 1536x1024 canvas. It shows the same small machine twice, seen from directly above, for a sci-fi strategy-game hardpoint (a heavy gun on a raised one-storey plinth; the plinth itself is NOT drawn, it is a separate layer underneath, and this one machine bolts onto its west wall). The machine is a single compact shield flux unit, a tall narrow slab about one by two: at its north end a capacitor as a smooth round pearl composite pod with a graphite ring and a round glass core, ringed by six small round charge-lamp sockets; at its south end a radiator: seven slim translucent blue-tinted glass fin plates in a graphite well, in a smooth rounded capsule housing. Left frame: the unit COLD and idle: radiator fins dull unlit metal, the capacitor's core window dark. Right frame: the SAME unit, identical in every shape, at full charge just before overload: the radiator fins and the capacitor's core window glow with stored field energy, bright pale blue light shining through the glass fins and core, whitening to blue-white at the hottest middle, with a soft luminous blue haze. In BOTH frames the six charge-lamp sockets stay small, dark and unlit (they are lit separately in the game). Everything else in the right frame (housing, bolts, frame, sockets) stays exactly as in the left frame. Material and style: Hard-light field high-tech: pale pearl-grey composite armoured in fine hexagonal ceramic plates with thin dark seams, graphite frames, glass; luminous, clean, otherworldly. Image 2 is the hardpoint the unit bolts onto: material, palette and finish reference only, not layout. Straight 90-degree overhead orthographic camera, top-down like a strategy-game map sprite, no perspective tilt. Sun from the upper left. Hand-painted gritty science-fiction game-sprite look like Starsector, physical believable machinery (real radiator fins, a heavy capacitor housing, bolts), restrained palette, coarse readable detail that survives being shrunk to about 30 to 40 pixels per cell. Exactly one unit per frame, nothing else. No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no watermark, no UI, no plinth, no gun, no cables leaving the unit, no ground or terrain, no cast shadow outside the object, no extra slab, apron or border. Transparent background outside the silhouette (if transparency is impossible, a flat pure white background). Change only material, surface detail and subtle shading, never placement, size or silhouette.
